observation.visible_scene: A black steam-cleaner wand/nozzle, marked with a small white button, is held at a downward angle over a herringbone-patterned tile floor beside a white baseboard. A visible plume of steam/vapor billows from the nozzle tip and drifts across the tiles throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The nozzle tip moves back and forth along a diagonal grout seam: it sits mid-frame early on, travels up toward the wall base (around frames 24-30), returns down (frames 31-35), and climbs up again toward the baseboard (frames 36-41).
The steam cloud continuously changes shape and position, expanding and diffusing around the nozzle and drifting toward the upper-left.
The wand's tilt and the apparent position of its white button shift slightly as the nozzle translates along the seam.
The framing of the tiles and the white baseboard changes subtly across the sequence, consistent with a slight camera pan/tilt, while the overall tile layout stays broadly recognizable.
outside_clip_unknowns: The operator, the steam-machine body, and the hand holding the wand are not visible.
Whether the floor is actually being cleaned or the tiles' appearance changes as a result is not shown within this segment.
The motion before frame 1 and after frame 41 is unknown; the excerpt is a mid-action crop.
uncertain_details: Exact camera motion is uncertain because the background tile pattern shifts only slightly; the apparent change in framing could be a small pan/tilt or the nozzle's movement relative to a near-static camera.
The precise cleaning effect on the grout/tiles cannot be confirmed from these frames alone.
